reading.rtitle: Casa Lume -- thank you for Friday night
paras: Dear Mr. Leão, thank you for your visit last Friday. It was a special night for us, and we want to share it with you.
There were forty guests, from nine different countries. There was one long table in the garden, and there were candles everywhere.
There was a band from Lisbon, and after dinner a lot of guests danced. There wasn't a free seat in the restaurant all night.
The kitchen made five dishes. There was fresh fish from the morning market, and there were three desserts — the chocolate cake was the favorite.
At eleven there was a toast for our chef, because it was his birthday. He was very happy, and a little red.
We hope you liked the night. There is a new dinner in the garden next month, and you are our guest again.

listenings.text: Last summer I went to my cousin's wedding in a small town in Italy. The dinner was in an old farm on a hill. There were more than a hundred guests, and there were long tables under the trees, with candles and flowers. There was no menu. The food came and came: pasta, fish, meat, cheese. There were five desserts, and I tried all of them. There was a band, of course, and everybody danced, from the grandmothers to the children. At midnight there was a toast for the couple, and there were fireworks over the hill. I didn't sleep, and I didn't care.

When I was a boy, I went to my grandmother's house every summer. It was in a small town near the sea. There was one street, and there were only twenty houses on it. There wasn't a supermarket, but there was a small market on Saturdays. There weren't many cars, so the children played in the street all day. There was a big tree in front of her house, and in the evening there were always people under it, talking. Today there is a big hotel there, and the tree is not there anymore. But in my head, the street is the same.
